Write a NumPy file

Source: R/read.R
npy_write.Rd

Encodes x as npy_encode() does and writes it to a path or a connection: an array, a data frame or another value as a .npy, a named list as a .npz.

Usage

npy_write(x, file, ...)

Arguments

x

The value to write; see npy_encode().

file

A path or a connection.

...

Further arguments of npy_encode(): dtype, order, na, encoding, unit and compress.

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

A path is overwritten. A connection that is not open is opened in binary mode and closed again; an open one must be binary and is left open.

See also

npy_read().

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".npz")
npy_write(list(a = 1:3, b = c("x", "y")), f, compress = TRUE)
npy_names(f)
#> [1] "a" "b"
str(npy_read(f))
#> List of 2
#>  $ a: int [1:3] 1 2 3
#>  $ b: chr [1:2] "x" "y"
unlink(f)
